references.text: John 13:26 fulfills the prophecy in Psalm 41:10 that a close friend who has shared bread with me has lifted his heel against me. The act of dipping the bread and giving it to Judas is the direct fulfillment of this betrayal.
In Matthew 26:23-25, the same moment is recounted where Jesus identifies the betrayer by giving him the bread, and Judas confirms his identity with the question: "Is it I, Rabbi?".
Mark 14:20 describes Jesus responding that it is one of the twelve who dips with him in the bowl, and that he will be betrayed by someone eating with him.
Luke 22:21-22 mentions that the hand of the one who betrays him is on the table with him, and that the Son's path is set, even though it is the path of the one who betrays him.
In John 17:12, Jesus refers to Judas as "the son of perdition" so that Scripture might be fulfilled, which connects directly to the identification and action in 13:26.
